previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fevers, chills, left flank pain, and a dislodged percutaneous nephrostomy (PCN) tube, following several weeks of cloudy, foul-smelling urine. He had recently completed a course of meropenem for a prior kidney infection. The PCN tube was replaced in the ED, and he was started on IV meropenem for pyelonephritis. Urine cultures from the PCN site initially grew E. coli, which was sensitive to meropenem; subsequent cultures showed no growth, indicating treatment success. An MRI of the left hip was performed due to concern for osteomyelitis from a chronic ulcer, but findings were consistent with reactive changes rather than bone infection, so no additional antibiotics were given. The patient declined professional wound care and opted to manage the ulcer himself. He also reported maroon blood in loose stools; rectal exam revealed hemorrhoids and prolapse without active bleeding, and no C. diff testing was completed due to inadequate sample. His chronic kidney disease remained stable, though phosphorus was elevated, suggesting a need for sevelamer dose adjustment post-discharge. He completed a 10-day course of meropenem and was discharged home on his prior medications, including oxycodone and fosfomycin, with naloxone provided for overdose prevention. Follow-up was arranged with nephrology, urology, and primary care.

PATIENT SUMMARY:
====================
___ yo M w/ paraplegia, and b/l indwelling PCN tubes, and h/o

mixed bacterial flora. He was treated with a 5 day course of IV 
meropenem as recommended by ID and then transitioned to PO 
fosfomycin q48h for additional 3 doses. Upon hearing this 
recommendation, the patient became very agitated and 
frustrated. He became verbally combative toward staff and 
requested to stay in the hospital for a longer course of IV 
antibiotics, despite our explanation that a longer course may 
increase his risk of growing resistant organisms without 
providing a clear benefit. He continued to exhibit abusive 
behavior and eventually left agitated prior to completion of 
discharge paperwork, and did not receive discharge paperwork. 
He did accept his script of fosfomycin. Further, his mother was 
contacted to update her on the discharge plan, and a script for 
fosfomycin was also faxed to his pharmacy.

PROCEDURE:
1. Left diagnostic antegrade nephrostogram.
2. Left 8 ___ nephrostomy exchange.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient.The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed prone
on the exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___ protocol.
The left prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.

Diluted contrast was injected into the left nephrostomy to confirm catheter
position. The image was stored on PACS. Local anesthesia was administered with
instillation of lidocaine jelly and 1% subcutaneous lidocaine injection. The
catheter was cut. A ___ wire was advanced into the left nephrostomy tube
and advanced into the distal ureter.  The catheter was removed over the wire.
A new 8 ___ nephrostomy catheter was flushed and advanced with its plastic
stiffener over the wire into appropriate position. The wire and stiffener were
removed and the pigtail was formed. Contrast injection confirmed appropriate
positioning. The final image was saved. The catheter was then flushed, stay
sutures applied and the catheter was secured with a Stat Lock device and
sterile dressings.  The catheter was attached to a bag for drainage.
The patient tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate
post-procedure complications.

FINDINGS:


1. Left antegrade nephrostogram shows obstruction at the level of the proximal
ureter.
2. Appropriate final position of left 8 ___ nephrostomy tube.

IMPRESSION: 

Technically successful left 8 ___ nephrostomy exchange.
